video_title: All The Market Tinder Needs Is A Spark To Crash | New Harbor Financial
gist: New Harbor's Mike Preston and John Lodra read last week's sharp AI/election-driven selloff as a likely 'rogue wave' and plan to nudge equity from 37.5% toward at most ~50% into a year-end drift higher, while warning that extreme valuations set the tinder for a disruptive, downward-biased 2027. Gold and silver hold three-day island reversals 'by their fingernails' against a hot CPI, Fed hikes and a breaking-out dollar; Bitcoin needs ~$84K (IBIT 47) before they'd buy.

themes.theme: Post-selloff positioning: rogue wave vs. top

insights.claim: New Harbor judges the recent largest-in-years one-day S&P/NASDAQ drop (Nov 5) as 70-80% likely a 'rogue wave' that loads negativity to push markets higher, since breadth and bullish-percent signals are flipping to buy on all main indices except the NASDAQ.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Systematic breadth signals favor buying the dip into year-end rather than de-risking.
insights.quote: I'm going to say that it's 70 or 80% likely at this point that that was a a rogue wave

insights.claim: After the selloff the NASDAQ sliced through its 200-day moving average and has only bounced back to its 21-day moving average, so it warrants more caution than the S&P, which nearly recovered the whole down bar.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Watch whether NASDAQ reclaims its 50-day; until then tech is the weakest link.

insights.claim: New Harbor's model cut equity from about 50% to 37.5% via stop-outs in real estate, regional banks and a 5% energy (XES) position sold near 96 after crude fell from about $100 to $84; XES then rebounded to 100.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Disciplined stops cost some whipsaw but are the price of risk control; the oil drop is hitting energy names.
insights.quote: There's no way to have risk control and and not have that happen from time to time.

insights.claim: New Harbor plans to raise equity from 37.5% into the low 40s and at most about 50%, favoring leaders like small caps and banks (XLF), which is back at its base breakout with strong relative strength despite a bearish engulfing bar.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Small caps and financials are the relative-strength leaders a systematic manager is adding to.

insights.claim: Even with green signals New Harbor caps equity near 50% because the market is severely overvalued and at the tail end of a big move, likely trying to find a top, though a blow-off parabola higher remains possible.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Size risk to the cycle stage: participate in a melt-up but don't go all-in at extreme valuations.
insights.quote: know where you are in the story

insights.claim: Adam Taggart argues the selloff was narrative-driven: after a 'blue wave' election, progressive candidates with anti-data-center or slow-the-buildout platforms spooked an AI-dependent market, and everything got flushed, not just tech.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Political pushback on data-center buildout is now a live risk factor for AI-linked equities.

insights.claim: John Lodra expects the market to drift or melt higher into year-end based on New Harbor's dashboard, but explicitly discounts seasonal averages such as strong post-midterm periods because dispersion around averages can hurt clients.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Lean bullish into year-end, but on signals rather than seasonality.
insights.quote: we are biased to think that markets are going to kind of uh either drip or or or melt higher

insights.claim: Per FactSet data (via Financial Times), S&P information technology fell from +31% YTD on October 5 to about +9.5% YTD by November 5, while long-dead consumer staples and healthcare surged in a month.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Violent sector rotation out of tech into defensives signals a fragile, late-stage tape.

insights.claim: Only about 12% of semiconductor stocks were on point-and-figure buy signals, a washed-out contrarian extreme that historically precedes sharp short-term rallies; the semis bullish percent has just reversed up.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Expect a relief rally in semis; holders wanting out may get a better exit in coming days or weeks.
insights.quote: only about 12% of stocks in the semiconductor sector were

insights.claim: New Harbor is underweight tech but warns against writing the sector off and piling into staples, because moves this fast risk whipsaw.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Don't chase the rotation into staples; fast reversals often whipsaw.

insights.claim: Information technology and communication services together were nearly 48-50% of the S&P a few weeks ago, so 'diversified' index investors are heavily exposed to the AI trade whether they realize it or not.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Passive S&P exposure is a concentrated AI bet; check real sector exposure.

insights.claim: Adam Taggart lists stacking AI risks: open/free models cannibalizing business models, circular financing, public pushback, heavy debt loads, real-world limits like permits, water and skilled labor, and the head of Nvidia being caught up in a reported scandal, even though compute demand still outstrips supply.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Demand indicators remain strong, but watch for any one of these risks to start mattering.
insights.quote: it just does seem that there just keeps stacking risk upon risk upon risk upon risk in this space

insights.claim: News of a large European bank panic-selling a big private credit loan portfolio coincided with the selloff, and the drop may partly reflect a big leveraged player forced to liquidate.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Private credit stress and forced liquidations are a potential spark to monitor.

insights.claim: CoreWeave, a poster child for AI froth, reported strong results and rallied, but John Lodra warns that if tech rallies to resistance and peters out, a cascading breakdown in breadth could set up a very challenging 2027.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Watch whether the tech relief rally fails at resistance as an early 2027 warning.

themes.theme: 2027 outlook: tinder set for a crash

insights.claim: New Harbor sees a very material likelihood of a disruptive, volatile, downward-biased stock market in 2027, with extreme valuations as the tinder and an unknown, likely nested series of sparks as the trigger.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Plan now to reduce vulnerability heading into 2027 despite near-term bullish signals.
insights.quote: Valuations are just one where the the tinder has been set. It's the spark just needs to happen

insights.claim: Major tops (tech bust, housing bust) follow a pattern of swift selloffs, a quick sigh of relief and a face-ripping rally that psychologically entraps investors who think the danger is over.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Treat sharp rebounds after shock drops in a toppy market as possible traps, not all-clears.
insights.quote: You get this face ripping rally that has you thinking that um that was just an emotional driven thing.

insights.claim: Jim Carson (as relayed by Adam Taggart) predicts strong year-end inflows and a rally, then the wheels coming off in Q1 2027, likely January, with a drop severe enough to force Fed and possibly Treasury intervention.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: A specific timing call: year-end strength, then January risk-off and policy intervention.

insights.claim: Household portfolios have the highest equity allocation ever, and most concerningly boomers, who should hold the least, have the highest equity ratio after markets rose almost 20% a year since 2022.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Record retail equity exposure magnifies drawdown risk and forced selling in a downturn.

insights.claim: Investors should set return targets from their financial plan rather than benchmark against the S&P; someone needing only 5% a year may be better off in a bond-heavy portfolio.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Match risk to required return, especially given elevated market risk now.
insights.quote: You might only need a 5% annual return

insights.claim: Risk is dynamic, not constant: the market is objectively riskier at some times than others, contrary to textbook assumptions.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Adjust exposure with the risk regime rather than holding a static allocation.
insights.quote: There is a thing called dynamic risk.

themes.theme: Fed hikes, CPI shock and the yield curve

insights.claim: A hot CPI print (0.4% versus Fed governor Waller's stated 0.3% threshold for a possible 50bp hike) pushed CME FedWatch to 100% odds of a hike at the December 9 meeting from a 3.75-4% target range, with rising odds of 50bp and of more hikes in early 2027.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Rate-hike risk is rising; rate-sensitive assets like gold and Bitcoin face near-term pressure.

insights.claim: Fed official Goulby (as spelled in captions) described the hot CPI report as 'borderline disturbing', and the Kevin Forch-led Fed (caption spelling) has already started hiking again this year.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: The Fed is in a hiking regime; don't assume cuts are near.

insights.claim: If the Fed hikes short rates enough to quell sticky-inflation fears, long-term yields could fall and long bonds rally, breaking the assumption that Fed hikes lift the whole curve.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: A credible hawkish Fed could set up a long-duration bond rally.
insights.quote: that causes long-term rates to drop because the market is then that much less worried about inflation being persistent

insights.claim: Oil is the big wild card for inflation; crude has fallen dramatically in recent weeks on geopolitical headlines, weakening energy stocks.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Oil headlines drive both inflation expectations and energy-sector stops.

themes.theme: Precious metals: hanging on by fingernails

insights.claim: Gold (GLD) has formed a three-day island reversal that took out the July lows; it holds as long as that low holds and the gap does not fill, and silver shows a similar three-day island after a 60%, nine-plus-month pullback.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: The island lows are the line in the sand for metals bulls.
insights.quote: They're hanging gold and silver are hanging on by their fingernails.

insights.claim: The dollar is breaking out of a cup-and-handle base near 103, and a stronger dollar on rising rate-hike expectations is a short-term headwind for gold; Mike Preston thinks the dollar can reach 108-110, the level Brent Johnson flagged as dangerous.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Dollar strength toward 108-110 is a risk to metals and global markets.

insights.claim: Gold must get back above $4,400-4,500 for New Harbor to say the bottom is likely in; short covering has not started yet and could add several hundred dollars an ounce quickly.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: A move above $4,400-4,500 is the confirmation trigger; short covering could make it violent.

insights.claim: Royal Gold (RGLD), the second-largest streaming company, broke out of a base and is challenging its January highs while gold and silver languish, showing strong relative strength among leading gold miners.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Miner relative strength can lead the metals; RGLD is a name to watch.

insights.claim: New Harbor holds about 11.5% in gold, silver bullion and miners, has recently shifted the mix toward bullion over miners based on relative strength, and admits it trimmed around the top but not enough.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Hold a core metals position sized to survive volatility rather than trading out tactically.
insights.quote: Hold your position at a size that you can hold it financially and psychologically.

insights.claim: New Harbor's long-term targets are $6,000+ gold and a new high in silver of $150+ over the next couple of years.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Implies large upside from current levels if the thesis plays out.

insights.claim: Dominic Frisbee's case for gold: US debt went from a third of GDP in 1980 to over 120% (near 200% with contingent liabilities), so a Volcker-style 20% rate would make interest exceed tax receipts, meaning rates can't defend the dollar and money printing follows.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Fiscal dominance argues for structural gold exposure and dollar-cost averaging into weakness.
insights.quote: Rates can't go high enough to defend the dollar, which means money printing.

insights.claim: Citing Ray Dalio's study of past reserve-currency empires (Dutch, Portuguese, Spanish, French, British), John Lodra argues indebted reserve issuers inflate debt away rather than default, making precious metals an important if bumpy long-term hedge.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Supports holding metals as a long-term debasement hedge despite short-term technicals.
insights.quote: You figure out a way to inflate it away.

insights.claim: Bitcoin at about $73,700 has erased its whole inverse head-and-shoulders breakout move from $65,000 to $125,000 after bottoming near $60,000; New Harbor holds none.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Bitcoin is in a failed-breakout state; patience over bottom-fishing.

insights.claim: New Harbor would only get tactically bullish on Bitcoin above about $84,000 (about 47 on IBIT), then sees a possible run to around $150K over the next year, roughly in step with gold reaching its targets.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Use $84K/IBIT 47 as the trigger to add; investors already heavy in bullion may not need it.
insights.quote: see if we can get back above 84,000 Bitcoin, 47 IBIT

insights.claim: Mike Preston rejects the 'Bitcoin went nowhere for five years at $74K' argument as cherry-picking, comparing it to the S&P being at 666 in March 2009, the same as 1996, which was still a great buy.
insights.speaker: Mike Preston
insights.so_what: Flat multi-year returns alone don't invalidate a buy.

insights.claim: Year-end priorities include taking required minimum distributions (a 50% penalty on under-distributed amounts) and Roth conversions to fill lower tax brackets as a tax arbitrage.
insights.speaker: John Lodra
insights.so_what: Act before year-end deadlines to avoid penalties and capture bracket arbitrage.
